title: alia-* alias migration map
appliesTo: epic #139, workstream 4. Required by docs/migration/compatibility-window.md section (a), removal gate 2.
notes: ADR 0003 says each of the thirteen aliases is either a CONCRETE MODEL REFERENCE or a ROUTING PROFILE, and is not a model owned by Alia. This file records which, per alias, with the measurement behind it.

All thirteen are routing profiles. None is a concrete model reference. The discriminator is fan-out: an identifier that resolves to one model is a reference to that model; one that picks among several is a policy. Every alias here fans out to at least two distinct upstream models operated by at least two distinct providers, so answering a request under any of them can substitute different weights than the previous request used.

distinctModels and distinctProviders are counted over TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS for the alias's tier and are not hand-typed: aliasMigrationMap.test.ts recomputes both from the live tables and fails if either moves. Change the routing and this file must change with it.

becomes.id is derived from the alias's own tier, because the tier IS the policy: TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS[tier] is the ranked candidate list the fallback engine walks. It is written in the product's own namespace with a profile: prefix, never in <publisher>/<model> form, per ADR 0003's routing-profile identity rule. The product-facing NAMES of these profiles belong to workstream 5, which owns the catalogue's type split; nothing here settles what the picker calls them.

PUBLISHER IS NOT RECORDED, and that is a finding rather than an omission. ADR 0003 makes the publisher the first segment of a model identity, but the mapping table stores a bare provider model id with no publisher segment (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v3`), so publisher is not recoverable from this repository's data without attributing each id by hand. Attribution belongs to Relay's catalogue, which is where model identity moves.

TWO ALIASES SHARE ONE POLICY. alia-v1-thinking and alia-v1-pro-max both carry tier v1-pro-max, so they are the same routing profile under two identifiers — the case ADR 0002 describes as a reasoning setting wearing a model's name. They are recorded separately because both are live identifiers a caller may hold, and both translate to the same replacement.

TWO TIERS HAVE NO ALIAS. v1-tts and v1-image exist in TIER_MODEL_MAPPINGS and no alias points at them; they are reached through the audio and image routes, not by naming a model. They are out of scope here because this file maps ALIASES, and nothing translates to them.
This file does not change what any alias resolves to. It describes.

sunsetAt is the removal date the product owner set on 2026-08-18, closing section (a) of the compatibility window after its usage gate was found unsatisfiable (production parked at desired count 0, no database credential outside it). It is NOT a placeholder: it is a decision with an owner, recorded in compatibility-window.md and epic-139-decisions.md D1. The value is the close of the first full calendar month after the announcement, because RFC 8594 section 3 requires the timestamp to be in the future and defines a past one as 'unavailable at any time', which would be false while every alias still resolves. It is asserted equal to ALIAS_SUNSET in packages/api/src/middleware/alias-deprecation.ts by aliasMigrationMap.test.ts, so the map and the header cannot disagree.
derivedFrom: packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/alia-models.ts:61-223 (ALIA_MODELS: the alias set and each alias's tier)

aliases.evidence: alia-models.ts:62-74 gives tier 'lite'; generate-model-mappings.ts ranks 15 distinct models across 13 providers. Recounted 2026-08-23 after Groq's llama-3.3-70b-versatile row was repointed at openai/gpt-oss-20b: Groq no longer serves any llama-3.3 id (404 model_not_found, measured), and gpt-oss-20b was already in this tier as a priority-17 stopgap, so the two rows collapsed into one and the tier lost the versatile id. Provider count is unchanged because Groq keeps a route.
alia-models.ts:75-87 gives tier 'v1'; generate-model-mappings.ts:54-72 ranks 17 distinct models across 14 providers.

alia-models.ts:136-147 gives tier 'v1-audio'; generate-model-mappings.ts:127-131 ranks 3 distinct models across 2 providers. The narrowest case on this page: all three are transcription models, but whisper-large-v3, whisper-large-v3-turbo and whisper-1 are three DIFFERENT models, so selecting between them is cross-model substitution and not a deployment choice.
